overview.title: The wider protected landscape
overview.p1: Ifrane National Park covers a broad Middle Atlas area of cedar forest, oak woodland and high plateaus. It is the larger natural frame behind the town, the lakes and the monkey forest stops.
overview.p2: You do not need a multi-day trek to feel it — short trails and scenic drives already show the park’s character. For longer hikes, local guides help with routes and seasons.
overview.p3: Respect fire rules, stay on paths and give wildlife space. The park’s value is in remaining a working ecosystem, not only a viewpoint list.

q1.question: Do I need a ticket?
q1.answer: Access rules vary by trailhead — check locally for any fees or guidance requirements.

q2.question: Hard hikes?
q2.answer: Options range from short walks to longer trails; pick honestly for your group.

q3.question: Best season?
q3.answer: Late spring and autumn for mild walking weather.

q4.question: Guide useful?
q4.answer: Yes for longer routes and deeper forest context.

q5.question: Combine with town?
q5.answer: Yes — park half-day and Ifrane evening works well.

food.title: Eat on a park day
food.p1: Carry water and a packed lunch for longer trails. Town restaurants wait at the end.
food.p2: Never leave food waste on trails.
